c_t_rule: c_t = c_s (prior: a strong reaction moves the same fraction of a group's mobilisable pool as of its persuadable pool); no data identify c_t before early votes and the weekly filter

uncertainty.form: each simulated election multiplies the switching and turnout parts of every story effect by its own factor, lognormal with mean 1 (the fitted size on average) and the spread below; the same factors for all races in that election

c_s.why: the fit itself is tight (0.19-0.23 leaving any one event out), but it is carried from big national events measured in approval and the generic ballot to state races, today's news and the harness's attention weights; about a factor of two either way covers that transfer

c_t.why: no data measure it before early votes; a wider range, which also covers the 0.05 first suggested

lasting_rule: Matteo, 28-29 Sep: news fades fast. Every story fades from the day it is first seen with a 5.5-day half-life, the single curve closest to Matteo's 45% after a week, 15% after two and under 10% after three (41%, 17%, 7%; 2% by day 30). A one-off story (endorsements, scandals, debates, ads, candidates' policy news, other) that drops out of the news also fades within about a day (half_life_days: 1 day from last_seen). Lasting topics (economy: prices, jobs, gas; national: president, Congress, war, disasters) don't get that drop and keep fading at the age rate. The calibration events' shifts held longer (lasting_evidence); the weekly filter tests the rate against polls. The 3 Nov forecast counts what is expected to remain of each story then; forecast.json's today view counts today's effects.

lasting_evidence.how: shift on each later window minus days -7..-1, regressed through the origin on the days +5..+14 shift; the series events2 measured the events on (538 and VoteHub approval and generic-ballot averages)

from: simlab/events2.json: 45 real events 2017-2025 with national opinion shifts, days +5..+14 against -7..-1 (approval: 538 and VoteHub averages; generic ballot: 538 and VoteHub polls; Engine)
runs/events2_groups__glm.jsonl: GLM's support answers for the 28 groups, direct wording, two option orders (Engine, simlab/groupcalib.py)
simlab/pimu.json: national persuadable shares (CES 2018 and 2022 waves)
c_s.fit: python -m simlab.moves --fit: weighted least squares of measured shift on the §3.2 switching term

journey: derived/D/params.json (copied daily, with date and run_id)
derived/D/moves.json (group changes and each story's switching and turnout effect)
derived/D/forecast.json (per-election multipliers; each race's news block: effect, parts, win chance if weaker or stronger)

notes: dials start at 1; the weekly filter tunes the dials and the half-lives from 12 Oct
